author: Bay State News
title: Harvard women's lacrosse prepares for road game against No. 8 Yale
text:
Harvard women’s lacrosse will travel to New Haven to face No. 8 Yale in the first of three consecutive away games, according to an April 15 announcement from the team. The match is scheduled for a noon start and will be streamed live on ESPN+.
This matchup is significant as it marks the beginning of Harvard’s final stretch of regular season games, all on the road. The Crimson aims to rebound after a recent loss and build momentum heading into the postseason.
In their previous outing, Harvard took an early lead against Cornell with goals from Kate Gilliam and Charlotte Hodgson but ultimately fell short in a close contest, losing 13-11 after Cornell secured two late goals in the fourth quarter. Notable performances included Hodgson’s multiple goals and Cecila Batchelder’s key plays throughout the game.
Looking back at last year’s meeting with Yale, Caroline Mullahy reached her 200th career point during a game that saw Harvard fall to the Bulldogs by a score of 14-9 at Jordan Field. Mullahy has continued her strong form this season with 19 goals and 43 assists through thirteen games, placing her just eight points shy of matching her career best.
Key contributors this year include Charlotte Hodgson, who leads Harvard with 31 goals and has scored in all but one game so far this season. Grace Mullahy follows closely behind with 24 goals, while Callie Batchelder has tallied points consistently over recent matches and now leads the team in overall points.
The Crimson started last season ranked among the top teams nationally, recording notable wins over UAlbany, Navy, and UConn. Caroline Mullahy’s achievements included breaking program records for assists and becoming one of only fifteen players in NCAA history to record more than 150 career assists.
As they prepare for their upcoming challenge against Yale, Harvard also welcomes eight new members as part of its Class of 2029 recruiting class—three of whom received recognition in national rankings.
